thread.title: Dow Jones Up; Small Caps Near Intermediate Correction | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Up; Small Caps Near Intermediate Correction | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The major indexes, including the Dow Jones industrial average, repeated the bigger volatility seen on Wall Street last week, but the S&P 500 aimed to end a two-day sell-off. Defensive companies paced the upside in stocks today.
X Meanwhile, the S&P SmallCap 600 fell as much as 8% below its all-time peak of 1100, set on Aug. 27. That places the S&P 600 closer to the territory of an intermediate-level correction of 10% or more.
The S&P 600 dropped 10.5% from its 52-week highs in early February.
Chinese equity indexes got hammered overnight on increasing signs that the world's No. 2 economy may suffer from steep U.S. import tariffs. The Shanghai composite, which had been closed for a full week, dropped 3.7% and fell back below its 50-day moving average.
While the Nasdaq composite lost nearly 0.6% with less than half an hour to go in Monday's session, it was down as much as 1.7%. Apple ( AAPL ), which remains a true stock market leader, shaved its decline from 1.8% earlier in the day to less than 0.4%.
At 223.50, the iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, MacBook and digital services innovator remains above its fast-rising 50-day moving average. The megacap tech also is keeping most of its gains since clearing a fine base on base with a 194.30 buy point on July 25.
The S&P 500 fell as much as 0.8% early but rebounded for a gain of around 0.1%.
These Blue Chips On Wall Street Buck The Drop The Dow Jones industrial average edged 0.3% higher thanks to gains of 1 point or more by at least five of its 30 components, including Travelers ( TRV ), McDonald's ( MCD ) and Walgreens Boot Alliance ( WBA ).
Some health care issues have been showing more relative strength.
IBD Stock Of The Day In the managed care industry group, Centene ( CNC )fell 0.5% but traded just 3% below a 52-week peak of 148.24. Shares of the Medicaid and state children's health plan expert are up more than 42% year to date. The stock is also finding bullish support at the 50-day moving average.
Centene broke out of a shallow flat base at 112.52 in mid-April. A first or second test of the 50-day or 10-week moving average following the breakout can provide a follow-on buy opportunity. Centene also is forming a flat base.
However, keep in mind that the current market outlook got downgraded by IBD on Thursday. This means that the risk of losing money in new buys is now higher.
In the IBD 50, software and medical companies notched some of the day's biggest losses.
Abiomed ( ABMD ), the heart pump innovator, fell more than 3% and briefly nicked its 50-day moving average. The large-cap stock and member of IBD's Medical-Products industry group is 12% below a 459.75 peak.
Shares had surpassed a 436.52 correct entry point in a double bottom but did not get far. At the stock's recent new high, the breakout produced a gain of just 5%.
Medical Software Play Aims To Hold 50-Day Line Veeva Systems ( VEEV ), a major player in management operations software for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, dropped 3% after sliding nearly 10% last week. The stock is undercutting its 10-week moving average for the first time in two months.
But check an IBD daily chart , and you'll find that investors are trying to shore up support for Veeva shares near the 50-day moving average, a bullish development. The 50-day moving average, drawn in red, graphically plots a stock's average closing price over the past 50 trading sessions. A rising 50-day line is positive.
At 95.18, Veeva holds a nearly 13% profit for those who bought on the breakout past an 84.34 buy point in a seven-week double bottom in mid-August.
Veeva ranks No. 5 in the IBD 50 through Monday afternoon trading.
Elsewhere, U.S. government bond traders took a day off on the Columbus Day holiday. The yield on the benchmark Treasury 10-year note remained at 3.23%.
WTI crude oil futures cooled off 0.2% to $74.19 a barrel. Prices are up nearly 23% since Jan. 1.
